transcript.text: Alright everyone, let's get this pre-approval review started. Before I sign off on the final shoot plan, I need status checks from each of your departments. We've got a lot moving tonight at the Riverside Foundry — drone work, horses, pyrotechnics, and parking — and I want to make sure we're not missing anything before I give the green light. Who wants to go first?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical issue with the drone plan. I confirmed with the aviation-permit vendor this afternoon that the Riverside Foundry permit only allows a tethered drone, not a free-flying drone like the current draft calls for. The permit also requires a licensed drone operator to be listed on the plan. The vendor's confirmation is still sitting in the cinematography equipment file. We need to revise the drone setup before this plan gets approved.

transcript.text: I need to flag an animal-welfare issue with the horse work. My animal-welfare representative confirmed today that the horse may work for no more than 4 hours total, and must receive a 30-minute rest break after each 2-hour work block. The current draft plan calls for six hours of horse work, which exceeds this limit. I haven't yet added the confirmation to the animal-use worksheet, but we need to revise the horse work schedule before this plan gets approved.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical insurance issue with the pyrotechnics plan. I confirmed with the production insurer that pyrotechnic effects are excluded from this shoot's policy, while atmospheric haze is covered. The insurer requires that any effect substitution be recorded in the effects plan. We need to replace the pyrotechnic spark wall with an atmospheric haze effect — or another covered alternative — and document the substitution before this plan gets approved.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical location issue with the wrap time and parking window. I received the signed neighborhood filming permit this morning, and it requires production to wrap by exactly 10:00 PM — not 11:00 PM as the current draft calls for. The permit also keeps the street-parking closure valid only from 6:00 PM through 10:00 PM, not until 11:00 PM. I have not yet replaced the draft location sheet, but we need to revise both the wrap time and the parking window before this plan gets approved.
